answers.answer: Keep four tokens per gem color and all five gold. Reveal three nobles. Remove unrevealed nobles permanently from the game.
answers.evidence: Token Adjustments: 2 | 4 (remove 3 of each color) | 5 | 3; Setup: "Remove remaining noble tiles from the game -- they will not be used."

answers.answer: Three players: five gems per color, five gold, four nobles. Four players: seven gems per color, five gold, five nobles; two more per color and one more noble, with gold unchanged.
answers.evidence: Token Adjustments: 3 | 5 | 5 | 4; 4 | 7 | 5 | 5.

answers.answer: Shuffle all three development decks separately. Arrange a column with level 1 at bottom, level 2 middle, level 3 top. Reveal four cards per level, making a 3-by-4 market. The youngest starts; play proceeds clockwise.
answers.evidence: Setup: "Shuffle each ... separately"; "Level 1 at bottom, Level 2 in middle, Level 3 on top"; "Reveal 4 cards ... from each level." First Player: "The youngest player goes first. Play proceeds clockwise."

answers.answer: Choose exactly one action: take three different gem colors; take two of one color if at least four are available beforehand; reserve one development if holding fewer than three, taking one gold if available; or buy one face-up or previously reserved development. Taking gems and buying, or reserving and buying that card, cannot be combined on a turn.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: "must perform exactly one" of the four listed actions; buy "1 card you reserved on a previous turn."

answers.answer: All tokens you own must be visible to all players at all times.
answers.evidence: Token Hand Limit: "All tokens a player owns must be visible to all players at all times."

answers.answer: You may take two green from four, leaving two, but may not take two red from three. Check the threshold before taking. Neither gem-taking action permits gold.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: "at least 4 tokens in the supply before taking them"; both gem-taking actions state "no gold."

answers.answer: Temporarily holding twelve is allowed. Return two tokens to finish with ten, and those may include the gems just drawn. Gold counts toward the limit.
answers.evidence: Token Hand Limit: "may temporarily exceed 10 during their action"; return chosen tokens "until they have exactly 10"; "including gold"; "may return some or all of the tokens they just took."

answers.answer: Take one gold, temporarily reaching eleven, then return one token of your choice to finish with ten. That token may be the gold just received. If the gold supply is empty, still reserve the card, receive no gold, and remain at ten.
answers.evidence: Reserve: "If no gold tokens remain, you may still reserve a card but receive no gold." Token Hand Limit: tokens returned may include "gold obtained by reserving."

answers.answer: Reserve a face-up market development or the top card of any one development deck. Do not show a deck card to opponents. Only the player who reserved the card can buy it.
answers.evidence: Reserve: "A face-up development card from the 3x4 grid" or "The top card from any one of the three level decks, without revealing it"; "Reserved cards may only be purchased by the player who reserved them."

answers.answer: You cannot reserve with three reserved cards, even just to obtain gold. You cannot discard or exchange a reserved card to make room; it can leave your hand only by being purchased.
answers.evidence: Reserved Cards: "If a player already has 3, they cannot reserve another"; "The only way to remove a reserved card from your hand is to purchase it."

answers.answer: Immediately replace the reserved level-2 market card with the top card of the level-2 deck. Purchasing a face-up card follows the same replacement rule. Buying a reserved card creates no market vacancy and needs no replacement. An empty relevant deck leaves the market space empty for the rest of the game.
answers.evidence: Card Replacement: "Whenever a face-up card is acquired (purchased) or reserved from the grid, it is immediately replaced by the top card of the same level’s deck"; if that deck is empty, "the empty space in the grid remains empty for the rest of the game."

answers.answer: Spend one green token, or a gold substituting for it; no blue tokens are needed. If bonuses cover every required color, spend no tokens. Bonuses are permanent and are not spent.
answers.evidence: Payment rules give the exact two-blue/one-green example: "you only need to spend 1 green token"; gold substitutes for "any single gem token"; enough bonuses allow purchase "without spending any tokens at all." Bonuses are "permanent."

answers.answer: Yes. The bonuses leave a cost of one blue, one black, and one white. Pay the blue token for blue and the two gold for black and white. Return all three spent tokens to the supply. Keep the bonus cards and their permanent bonuses.
answers.evidence: Payment rules: bonuses reduce costs; gold "can substitute for any single gem token"; "Spend the required gem tokens, returning them to the supply"; "Spent gold tokens are returned to the supply." Bonus Stacking says each bonus is added "permanently."

answers.answer: You may buy a face-up market development or a previously reserved development from your own hand. Place acquired cards face-up in front of you, sorted by bonus color and staggered to keep bonuses and prestige values visible to everyone at all times.
answers.evidence: Purchase: "a face-up development card from the grid or a previously reserved card from your hand"; "sorted by bonus color and staggered so that bonuses and prestige point values are visible to all players at all times."

answers.answer: No: two white bonuses are insufficient, and neither a white token nor gold substitutes for the third bonus. Acquiring a third white bonus qualifies you at the end of the turn. Bonuses above requirements do not disqualify you.
answers.evidence: Noble Visits: "at least the quantity and types of bonuses"; "bonuses only ... not gem tokens." Noble Tile Mechanics: "having more is fine."

answers.answer: Choose one noble. You cannot take both or refuse all visits. Receiving it takes no action and gives three prestige. Eligibility is checked at the end of your turn after the action.
answers.evidence: Noble Visits: "automatic -- a player cannot refuse it"; "not an action"; "choose one"; "at most one noble per turn"; "3 prestige points"; "At the end of their turn."

answers.answer: Place its tile face-up in front of you.
answers.evidence: Noble visit rules: "Place the received noble tile face-up in front of you."

answers.answer: C and D still take a turn; A does not get another turn. B is not guaranteed to win because the highest prestige at the end of the final round determines the winner.
answers.evidence: End-Game Trigger: "the current round is completed so that every player has played the same number of turns." End-of-Game Clarifications: "A player who triggers the end game may not necessarily win."

answers.answer: Your new total is sixteen. This triggers the end game because fifteen or more qualifies, even when skipping fifteen. Finish the current round, then determine the winner by highest prestige and the tiebreaker if needed.
answers.evidence: Noble tiles: "3 each." End-Game Trigger: "15 or more prestige points." Determining the Winner: "most prestige points at the end of the final round."

answers.answer: B wins. A and B tie for highest prestige at sixteen, and B has nine purchased developments versus A’s ten. C’s lower prestige excludes C despite fewer cards. Nobles count toward prestige. B’s three cards still reserved are not purchased developments and do not count toward that tiebreaker.
answers.evidence: Determining the Winner: "most prestige points"; "Noble tile points count toward the total." Tiebreaker: "fewest development cards" purchased. Reserved Cards distinguishes held reserves from purchasing them.
